Your home office wherever makes you happiest • Professional growth: Time built in to try new tools on real problems and share what you find. People here want to see you grow, and they'll jump in when you're stuck Our values We hire for the same five values in every role at P3: • Reliable. You do what you said you'd do, and what you ship keeps working. • Adaptable. The tools change every month. You change with them, and you change course when a project stops making sense. • Proactive. Strong proficiency in React , Next.js , TypeScript/JavaScript. Hands-on experience with AWS for production workloads. Solid understanding of web security best practices (OWASP, secure storage, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets management). Experience building systems in or adjacent to healthcare, education, or compliance-heavy environments is a plus. Excellent async communication, code ownership, and ability to work with a small, senior-led team. Comfort working from a clear product brief and also proposing improvements proactively. Familiarity with logging, monitoring, and observability tools. Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process) Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare: Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n. Stack Next.js (App Router) Clerk for authentication Convex for data + backend logic n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation TypeScript Requirements Public page The fictional company name is LendLoop . Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.” Show: A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex. A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk. Authenticated experience Only signed-in users can: List a tool with: name category (power tools, garden, kitchen, camping, etc.) condition short description Request to borrow a tool for a date range. Approve or decline requests on their own tools. Mark a loan as returned. Show: All tools with availability status, filterable by category. “My listings”, “My requests”, and “Incoming requests” views. Nice, minimal layout. Roles & rules Have two roles: admin : Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”. user : Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing. Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI. Automation with n8n Build at least two n8n workflows: Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs. Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex. Secure the integration in both directions: Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side. Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON. Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders. Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently. (Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”. Deliverables A GitHub repository with the app source code. Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository. A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions. A short note on what you would change to run this in production. We evaluate: Code structure and clarity Security-minded thinking UX and practicality Integration design, reliability, and error handling (n8n) Documentation and reasoning Interview Process Take-home assignment submission (as described above). Technical & product interview (walkthrough of your solution, architecture, security mindset, collaboration style). 6-month contract offer for the right candidate, with strong potential for renewal as a recurring contract based on performance and ownership.
